    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join(self._lines)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "ScreenLines({0!r})".format(self._lines)

    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(other, str):
            return str(self) == other
        if isinstance(other, list):
            return self._lines == other
        if isinstance(other, _ScreenLines):
            return self._lines == other._lines
        return NotImplemented

    def __ne__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        result = self.__eq__(other)
        if result is NotImplemented:
            return result
        return not result

    __hash__ = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    # -- convenience -------------------------------------------------------
    def index(self, item, *args):  # noqa: A001 - mirror list.index
        return self._lines.index(item, *args)

    def count(self, item):
        return self._lines.count(item)


class _ScreenText(_CallableStr):
    """Rendered screen text that also exposes ``display`` / ``cursor``."""

    def __new__(
        cls,
        text: str,
        display: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
        cursor=None,
        columns: Optional[int] = None,
        lines: Optional[int] = None,
    ):
        obj = super().__new__(cls, text)
        obj.display = _ScreenLines(display or [])  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.cursor = cursor  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.columns = columns  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.lines = lines  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        return obj


_Cursor = namedtuple("Cursor", ["x", "y"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ANSI escape sequence handling (used to build a readable transcript)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(
    "\x1b(?:"
    r"\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\?)"  # OSC ... (BEL | ST)
    r"|\[[\x30-\x3f]*[\x20-\x2f]*[\x40-\x7e]"  # CSI ... final
    r"|[P78^_][^\x1b]*(?:\x1b\\)"  # DCS / SOS / PM / APC ... ST
    r"|[\x20-\x2f]*[\x30-\x7e]"  # any other escape sequence
    ")"
)

# Control characters that carry no meaning in a plain-text transcript.
_JUNK_CONTROL_RE = re.compile(r"[\x00\x07\x0b\x0c\x0e\x0f\x1a\x7f]")

_DEFAULT_PATH = "/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

_SPECIAL_KEYS: Dict[str, str] = {
    "enter": "\r",
    "return": "\r",
    "cr": "\r",
    "newline": "\r",
    "linefeed": "\n",
    "tab": "\t",
    "shift-tab": "\x1b[Z",
    "backtab": "\x1b[Z",
    "esc": "\x1b",
    "escape": "\x1b",
    "space": " ",
    "backspace": "\x7f",
    "bs": "\x7f",
    "delete": "\x1b[3~",
    "del": "\x1b[3~",
    "insert": "\x1b[2~",
    "home": "\x1b[H",
    "end": "\x1b[F",
    "begin": "\x1b[H",
    "up": "\x1b[A",
    "down": "\x1b[B",
    "right": "\x1b[C",
    "forward": "\x1b[C",
    "left": "\x1b[D",
    "back": "\x1b[D",
    "pageup": "\x1b[5~",
    "pgup": "\x1b[5~",
    "pagedown": "\x1b[6~",
    "pgdn": "\x1b[6~",
    "f1": "\x1bOP",
    "f2": "\x1bOQ",
    "f3": "\x1bOR",
    "f4": "\x1bOS",
    "f5": "\x1b[15~",
    "f6": "\x1b[17~",
    "f7": "\x1b[18~",
    "f8": "\x1b[19~",
    "f9": "\x1b[20~",
    "f10": "\x1b[21~",
    "f11": "\x1b[23~",
    "f12": "\x1b[24~",
}


def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove ANSI/VT escape sequences from *text*."""
    return _ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.sub("", text)


def _clean_output(data: bytes, encoding: str = "utf-8") -> str:
    """Turn raw pty output into a readable, newline-normalised transcript."""
    text = data.decode(encoding, "replace")
    text = _strip_ansi(text)
    text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    text = _JUNK_CONTROL_RE.sub("", text)
    return text


def _key_name_to_sequence(key: str) -> str:
    """Translate a key name such as ``"ctrl+c"`` or ``"enter"`` into the
    byte sequence a real terminal sends for that key."""
    name = str(key).strip().lower().replace("_", "+").replace("-", "+")
    if name in _SPECIAL_KEYS:
        return _SPECIAL_KEYS[name]
    if name.startswith("ctrl+") or name.startswith("control+") or name.startswith("c+"):
        prefix = "ctrl+" if name.startswith("ctrl+") else (
            "control+" if name.startswith("control+") else "c+"
        )
        ch = name[len(prefix):]
        if len(ch) == 1 and "a" <= ch <= "z":
            return chr(ord(ch) - 96)
        if len(ch) == 1 and "0" <= ch <= "9":  # Ctrl-@ .. Ctrl-_
            return chr((ord(ch) - ord("0") + 32) % 128)
        if ch == "space":
            return "\x00"
        if ch == "[":
            return "\x1b"
        if ch == "\\":
            return "\x1c"
        if ch == "]":
            return "\x1d"
        if ch == "^":
            return "\x1e"
        if ch == "_":
            return "\x1f"
        raise HeadlessTerminalError("unknown key: {0!r}".format(key))
    if name.startswith("alt+") or name.startswith("meta+") or name.startswith("esc+"):
        prefix_len = 4
        return "\x1b" + key.strip()[prefix_len:]
    # fall back: the key *is* the characters to type
    return str(key)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fallback screen (only used when pyte is not installed)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _FallbackScreen:
    """A very small VT-screen approximation used when ``pyte`` is missing.

    It understands plain text, carriage returns, line feeds, tabs and
    backspaces which is enough for ordinary command output.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int = 80, lines: int = 24):
        self.columns = columns
        self.lines = lines
        self._rows: List[List[str]] = [[" "] * columns for _ in range(lines)]
        self._x = 0
        self._y = 0
        self.cursor = _Cursor(0, 0)

    # -- api compatible with the parts of pyte we use ----------------------
    def feed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        text = _strip_ansi(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        for char in text:
            self._put(char)

    def resize(self, lines: Optional[int] = None, columns: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
        if lines is not None:
            self.lines = lines
        if columns is not None:
            self.columns = columns
        self._rows = [
            (self._rows[i] if i < len(self._rows) else [])[: self.columns]
            + [" "] * max(0, self.columns - len(self._rows[i] if i < len(self._rows) else []))
            for i in range(self.lines)
        ]
        self._x = min(self._x, self.columns - 1)
        self._y = min(self._y, self.lines - 1)
        self.cursor = _Cursor(self._x, self._y)

    @property
    def display(self) -> List[str]:
        return ["".join(row) for row in self._rows]

    # -- internals ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _put(self, char: str) -> None:
        if char == "\n":
            self._x = 0
            self._index()
        elif char == "\r":
            self._x = 0
        elif char == "\b":
            self._x = max(0, self._x - 1)
        elif char == "\t":
            self._x = min(self.columns - 1, (self._x // 8 + 1) * 8)
        elif char >= " ":
            if self._y >= len(self._rows):
                self._y = len(self._rows) - 1
            row = self._rows[self._y]
            if self._x >= len(row):
                row.extend([" "] * (self._x - len(row) + 1))
            row[self._x] = char
            self._x += 1
            if self._x >= self.columns:
                self._x = 0
                self._index()
        self.cursor = _Cursor(self._x, self._y)

    def _index(self) -> None:
        self._y += 1
        if self._y >= self.lines:
            self._rows.pop(0)
            self._rows.append([" "] * self.columns)
            self._y = self.lines - 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The terminal itself
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class HeadlessTerminal(BaseTerminal):
    """A headless terminal emulator running an interactive ``bash`` shell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    command:
        Program to run inside the terminal.  ``None`` (the default) starts
        an interactive ``bash`` shell.  A string is run with ``bash -i -c``
        and a list is used as the ``argv`` directly.
    cols, rows:
        Size of the terminal window (default 80x24).
    env:
        Extra environment variables merged over the current environment.
    cwd:
        Working directory for the shell.
    encoding:
        Encoding used to decode the terminal output (default ``utf-8``).
    term:
        Value of the ``TERM`` environment variable (default ``xterm-256color``).
    """

    # how long ``send_keystrokes`` keeps waiting for *late* output after the
    # requested ``wait_sec`` has elapsed (bounded!)
    _DRAIN_QUIET = 0.05
    _DRAIN_LIMIT = 0.6

    def __init__(
        self,
        command: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
        cols: Optional[int] = None,
        rows: Optional[int] = None,
        env: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
        cwd: Optional[str] = None,
        encoding: str = "utf-8",
        term: Optional[str] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()

        # -- forgiving keyword aliases ------------------------------------
        if cols is None:
            cols = kwargs.pop("columns", kwargs.pop("width", None))
        if rows is None:
            rows = kwargs.pop("lines", kwargs.pop("height", None))
        if command is None:
            command = kwargs.pop(
                "cmd",
                kwargs.pop("argv", kwargs.pop("shell", kwargs.pop("program", None))),
            )
        if env is None:
            env = kwargs.pop("environment", None)
        if cwd is None:
            cwd = kwargs.pop(
                "working_dir", kwargs.pop("workdir", kwargs.pop("directory", None))
            )
        if term is None:
            term = kwargs.pop("term_type", kwargs.pop("TERM", None))
        self._default_timeout = float(kwargs.pop("timeout", 10.0))
        # any other keyword arguments are ignored on purpose (forward
        # compatibility with alternative constructor signatures)

        self._cols = max(2, int(cols)) if cols else 80
        self._rows = max(2, int(rows)) if rows else 24
        self._encoding = encoding or "utf-8"
        self._bash_path = shutil.which("bash") or "/bin/bash"

        # -- state ----------------------------------------------------------
        self._raw = bytearray()          # every byte ever printed by the pty
        self._lock = threading.RLock()   # protects _raw / screen / stream
        self._exit_lock = threading.RLock()
        self._closed = False
        self._eof = False
        self._exit_status: Optional[int] = None
        self._master_fd: Optional[int] = None
        self._write_errors: List[BaseException] = []
        self._expect_pos = 0
        self._created_at = time.monotonic()

        child_env = self._build_env(env, term)
        argv = self._build_argv(command)

        pid, master_fd = pty.fork()
        if pid == 0:  # ----- child: becomes the interactive shell -----
            try:
                if cwd:
                    os.chdir(cwd)
                os.execve(argv[0], argv, child_env)
            except BaseException as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exec failure
                try:
                    os.write(
                        2,
                        "headless_terminal: cannot exec {0!r}: {1}\n".format(
                            argv, exc
                        ).encode("utf-8", "replace"),
                    )
                except OSError:
                    pass
            os._exit(127)

        # ----- parent -----
        self._pid = pid
        self._master_fd = master_fd
        try:
            self._set_winsize(self._rows, self._cols)
        except OSError:  # pragma: no cover
            pass

        # virtual screen: a real terminal emulator (with scrollback)
        if pyte is not None:
            self._screen = pyte.HistoryScreen(self._cols, self._rows, history=1000)
            self._stream = pyte.ByteStream(self._screen)
        else:  # pragma: no cover - pyte is a hard dependency normally
            self._screen = _FallbackScreen(self._cols, self._rows)
            self._stream = self._screen  # type: ignore[assignment]

        self._reader = threading.Thread(
            target=self._read_loop,
            name="headless-terminal-reader-{0}".format(pid),
            daemon=True,
        )
        self._reader.start()

        # give the shell a chance to start up, print its prompt and source
        # the startup files before the first keystrokes are sent
        self._wait_for_initial_output()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # BaseTerminal interface
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def send_keystrokes(self, keystrokes: str, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Send *keystrokes* to the terminal.

        Args:
            keystrokes: The keystrokes to send to the terminal.  Plain
                characters are typed literally; ``"\\n"`` (or ``"\\r"``) is
                the Enter key; control keys are sent as their control
                character (``"\\x03"`` = Ctrl-C, ``"\\x04"`` = Ctrl-D, ...)
                and escape sequences such as ``"\\x1b[A"`` (Up arrow) are
                passed through verbatim.
            wait_sec: The number of seconds to wait for the command to
                complete.
        """
        data = self._keystrokes_to_bytes(keystrokes)
        self._write(data)
        try:
            wait = float(wait_sec)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            wait = 0.0
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep(wait)
        # capture any output that is still in flight (bounded by a short
        # quiet period so this never hangs)
        self._drain(quiet=self._DRAIN_QUIET, limit=self._DRAIN_LIMIT)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Convenience wrappers around send_keystrokes
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def send(self, text: str, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Alias of :meth:`send_keystrokes`."""
        self.send_keystrokes(text, wait_sec=wait_sec)

    def sendline(self, line: str = "", wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Send *line* followed by the Enter key."""
        self.send_keystrokes("{0}\n".format(line), wait_sec=wait_sec)

    send_line = sendline
    send_command = sendline

    def type_text(self, text: str, delay: float = 0.02, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Type *text* one character at a time (with a small delay).

        Some interactive programs are happier when keys do not arrive in a
        single burst.
        """
        text = str(text)
        for index in range(len(text)):
            self._write(self._keystrokes_to_bytes(text[index]))
            if delay and index < len(text) - 1:
                time.sleep(delay)
        try:
            wait = float(wait_sec)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            wait = 0.0
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep(wait)
        self._drain(quiet=self._DRAIN_QUIET, limit=self._DRAIN_LIMIT)

    type = type_text

    def press(self, key: str, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Press a special key, e.g. ``press("ctrl+c")``, ``press("enter")``,
        ``press("up")`` or ``press("escape")``."""
        self.send_keystrokes(_key_name_to_sequence(key), wait_sec=wait_sec)

    def press_enter(self, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Press the Enter key."""
        self.press("enter", wait_sec=wait_sec)

    def interrupt(self, wait_sec: float = 0.5) -> None:
        """Send Ctrl-C (SIGINT)."""
        self.press("ctrl+c", wait_sec=wait_sec)

    def eof(self, wait_sec: float = 0.5) -> None:
        """Send Ctrl-D (EOF)."""
        self.press("ctrl+d", wait_sec=wait_sec)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reading the terminal
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def output(self) -> str:
        """Everything the terminal has printed so far (cleaned up: ANSI
        escape sequences removed, newlines normalised)."""
        with self._lock:
            raw = bytes(self._raw)
        return _CallableStr(_clean_output(raw, self._encoding))

    def get_output(self, clean: bool = True) -> str:
        """Return the terminal output; ``clean=False`` returns the raw
        undecorated bytes decoded as text (escape sequences included)."""
        if clean:
            return self.output
        with self._lock:
            raw = bytes(self._raw)
        return raw.decode(self._encoding, "replace")

    def read(self, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> str:
        """Return everything the terminal printed (like a file ``read()``).

        If *wait_sec* is given, first wait that long for more output.
        """
        if wait_sec:
            self._drain(quiet=self._DRAIN_QUIET, limit=float(wait_sec))
        return self.output

    read_all = read
    get_text = get_output

    def read_new(self, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> str:
        """Return only the output that appeared since the last
        :meth:`read_new` / :meth:`drain_new` call."""
        with self._lock:
            start = self._read_new_pos
            self._read_new_pos = len(self._raw)
        return _clean_output(bytes(self._raw[start:]), self._encoding)

    drain_new = read_new

    @property
    def raw_output(self) -> bytes:
        """The raw, untouched bytes written by the terminal."""
        with self._lock:
            return bytes(self._raw)

    @property
    def bytes(self) -> bytes:  # noqa: A003 - deliberate alias
        """Alias of :attr:`raw_output`."""
        return self.raw_output

    @property
    def lines(self) -> List[str]:
        """The transcript split into lines."""
        return self.output.split("\n")

    # -- the virtual screen --------------------------------------------
    @property
    def screen(self) -> str:
        """The current contents of the (80x24) screen, as text."""
        return self._render_screen()

    def get_screen(self, include_history: bool = False, rstrip: bool = True) -> str:
        """Return the rendered screen; optionally include scrollback."""
        return self._render_screen(
            include_history=include_history, rstrip=rstrip
        )

    def screenshot(self) -> str:
        """Alias of :meth:`get_screen`."""
        return self.get_screen()

    @property
    def display(self) -> _ScreenLines:
        """The rows of the virtual screen (indexable and iterable)."""
        return self.screen.display  # type: ignore[attr-defined,no-any-return]

    get_display = display

    @property
    def cursor(self) -> _Cursor:
        """Current cursor position ``(x, y)`` on the screen."""
        screen = self.screen
        cursor = getattr(screen, "cursor", None)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        if cursor is None:
            return _Cursor(0, 0)
        return _Cursor(int(cursor.x), int(cursor.y))

    def get_cursor_position(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Return the cursor position as a ``(x, y)`` tuple."""
        cursor = self.cursor
        return (cursor.x, cursor.y)

    @property
    def size(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Current ``(rows, cols)`` of the terminal window."""
        return (self._rows, self._cols)

    @property
    def dimensions(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Alias of :attr:`size`."""
        return self.size

    def resize(self, rows: Optional[int] = None, cols: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
        """Resize the terminal window."""
        if rows is not None:
            self._rows = max(2, int(rows))
        if cols is not None:
            self._cols = max(2, int(cols))
        if self._master_fd is not None:
            try:
                self._set_winsize(self._rows, self._cols)
            except OSError:  # pragma: no cover
                pass
        with self._lock:
            try:
                self._screen.resize(lines=self._rows, columns=self._cols)
            except TypeError:  # pragma: no cover - fallback screen
                self._screen.resize(self._rows, self._cols)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

    # -- waiting for output ---------------------------------------------
    def wait_for(self, pattern: str, timeout: Optional[float] = None):
        """Wait until *pattern* (a literal string) appears in the output."""
        return self.expect(re.escape(pattern), timeout=timeout)

    def expect(self, pattern, timeout: Optional[float] = None):
        """Wait until *pattern* (a regex or a literal string) appears in the
        output and return the match object.

        Raises :class:`TerminalTimeout` if the pattern does not show up in
        time.
        """
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = self._default_timeout
        if isinstance(pattern, re.Pattern):
            regex = pattern
        elif isinstance(pattern, (list, tuple)):
            regex = re.compile("|".join("(?:{0})".format(re.escape(p)) for p in pattern))
        else:
            regex = re.compile(str(pattern))

        start = self._expect_pos
        deadline = time.monotonic() + float(timeout)
        while True:
            text = self.output
            match = regex.search(text, start)
            if match is not None:
                self._expect_pos = match.end()
                return match
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise TerminalTimeout(
                    "pattern {0!r} not found in terminal output after {1}s".format(
                        pattern, timeout
                    )
                )
            time.sleep(0.02)

    def wait_for_quiet(self, quiet: float = 0.2, limit: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Wait until the terminal has been silent for *quiet* seconds."""
        self._drain(quiet=quiet, limit=limit)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Process management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def is_alive(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` while the shell (or its foreground program) is running."""
        if self._exit_status is not None:
            return False
        return self._reap() is None

    @property
    def alive(self) -> bool:
        """Alias of :meth:`is_alive`."""
        return self.is_alive()

    @property
    def pid(self) -> int:
        """Process id of the shell."""
        return self._pid

    @property
    def exit_status(self) -> Optional[int]:
        """Exit status of the shell (``None`` while it is still running)."""
        if self._exit_status is None:
            self._reap()
        if self._exit_status is None:
            return None
        status = self._exit_status
        if os.WIFEXITED(status):
            return os.WEXITSTATUS(status)
        if os.WIFSIGNALED(status):
            return -os.WTERMSIG(status)
        return status

    returncode = exit_status
    exit_code = exit_status

    def wait(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[int]:
        """Wait for the shell to exit and return its exit status."""
        deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
        while True:
            if self._reap(blocking_for=0.1) is not None:
                return self.exit_status
            if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                return None
            time.sleep(0.02)

    def terminate(self, timeout: float = 1.0) -> None:
        """Politely terminate the shell and everything it started."""
        self._signal_group(signal.SIGTERM)
        if self._reap(blocking_for=timeout) is None:
            self.kill()

    def kill(self) -> None:
        """Forcefully kill the shell and everything it started."""
        self._signal_group(signal.SIGKILL)
        self._reap(blocking_for=0.5)

    def close(self, timeout: float = 1.0) -> None:
        """Shut the terminal down and reap the shell process."""
        if self._closed:
            self._reap(blocking_for=0.1)
            return
        self._closed = True

        reader = getattr(self, "_reader", None)
        if reader is not None and reader.is_alive():
            reader.join(timeout=1.0)

        fd, self._master_fd = self._master_fd, None
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                os.close(fd)  # sends SIGHUP to the session
            except OSError:
                pass

        if self._reap(blocking_for=0.5) is None:
            self._signal_group(signal.SIGTERM)
            if self._reap(blocking_for=0.5) is None:
                self._signal_group(signal.SIGKILL)
                self._reap(blocking_for=0.5)

    shutdown = close
    stop = close

    # context manager ---------------------------------------------------
    def __enter__(self) -> "HeadlessTerminal":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:
        self.close()

    def __del__(self):  # pragma: no cover - best effort cleanup
        try:
            self.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        state = "closed" if self._closed else ("alive" if self.is_alive() else "exited")
        return "<HeadlessTerminal pid={0} size={1}x{2} {3}>".format(
            getattr(self, "_pid", None), self._cols, self._rows, state
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # internals
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build_argv(self, command) -> List[str]:
        if command is None:
            return [self._bash_path, "-i"]
        if isinstance(command, (list, tuple)):
            argv = [str(part) for part in command]

    def _drain(self, quiet: float = 0.05, limit: float = 0.5) -> None:

        last_size = len(self._raw)
        last_change = time.monotonic()

            time.sleep(0.01)
            now = time.monotonic()
            size = len(self._raw)
            if size != last_size:
                last_size = size
                last_change = now
                if now >= deadline:
                    return
                continue
            if now - last_change >= quiet or now >= deadline:

            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:

        if self._raw:
            self._drain(quiet=0.1, limit=1.0)

    def _render_screen(
        self, include_history: bool = False, rstrip: bool = True
    ) -> _ScreenText:
        with self._lock:

            cursor = getattr(self._screen, "cursor", None)
            columns = getattr(self._screen, "columns", self._cols)

can read works, including:

* plain text and ``"\\n"`` / ``"\\r"`` (the Enter key),
* control / modifier keys such as ``"\\x03"`` (Ctrl-C), ``"\\x04"`` (Ctrl-D),
  ``"\\x1a"`` (Ctrl-Z), ``"\\x15"`` (Ctrl-U), ``"\\x7f"`` (Backspace), ...
* escape sequences such as ``"\\x1b[A"`` (Up), ``"\\x1b[B"`` (Down),
  ``"\\x1b[C"`` (Right), ``"\\x1b[D"`` (Left), ``"\\t"`` (Tab, i.e.
  completion), ...  Cursor-key sequences are automatically translated to
  the ``SS3`` form (``"\\x1bOA"`` ...) while the foreground program has the
  terminal in *application cursor keys* mode (DECCKM), which is what a real
  terminal does and what full-screen programs (vim, less, curses, ...)
  expect.

Everything the terminal prints is read by a background thread and is:

* kept verbatim                      -> :attr:`raw_output`
* kept as a cleaned-up transcript    -> :attr:`output`
  (ANSI escape sequences removed, newlines normalised)
* rendered into a virtual screen (a real VTxxx terminal emulator, courtesy
  of ``pyte``)                       -> :attr:`screen` / :attr:`display`
  which is what makes full-screen interactive programs usable.

Example
-------
::

    from headless_terminal import HeadlessTerminal

    term = HeadlessTerminal()                     # interactive bash shell
    term.send_keystrokes("echo hello world\\n", wait_sec=1.0)
    assert "hello world" in term.output
    term.send_keystrokes("\\x03")                 # Ctrl-C
    term.close()
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helper types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _CallableStr(str):
    """A ``str`` that can also be *called* (returns itself).

    This lets attributes be used both as properties and as methods, e.g.
    ``term.output`` and ``term.output()`` both return the terminal output.
    """

    __slots__ = ()

    def __call__(self) -> str:  # noqa: D102 - see class docstring
        return self


class _ScreenLines:
    """A list-of-lines view of the screen that also behaves like text.

    * ``"text" in lines`` -> substring test (like text) *and* exact line test
    * ``lines[0]``        -> first screen row
    * ``iter(lines)``     -> iterates over the screen rows
    * ``str(lines)``      -> the whole screen as text
    """

    def __init__(self, lines: Iterable[str]):
        self._lines: List[str] = ["".join(line).rstrip() for line in lines]

    # -- sequence protocol -------------------------------------------------
    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._lines)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self._lines[index]

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._lines)

    def __contains__(self, item: Any) -> bool:
        if isinstance(item, str):
            return any(item in line for line in self._lines)
        return item in self._lines

    # -- text-ish protocol -------------------------------------------------
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join(self._lines)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "ScreenLines({0!r})".format(self._lines)

    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(other, str):
            return str(self) == other
        if isinstance(other, list):
            return self._lines == other
        if isinstance(other, _ScreenLines):
            return self._lines == other._lines
        return NotImplemented

    def __ne__(self, other: Any) -> Any:
        result = self.__eq__(other)
        if result is NotImplemented:
            return result
        return not result

    __hash__ = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    # -- convenience -------------------------------------------------------
    def index(self, item, *args):  # noqa: A001 - mirror list.index
        return self._lines.index(item, *args)

    def count(self, item):
        return self._lines.count(item)


class _ScreenText(_CallableStr):
    """Rendered screen text that also exposes ``display`` / ``cursor``."""

    def __new__(
        cls,
        text: str,
        display: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
        cursor=None,
        columns: Optional[int] = None,
        lines: Optional[int] = None,
    ):
        obj = super().__new__(cls, text)
        obj.display = _ScreenLines(display or [])  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.cursor = cursor  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.columns = columns  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        obj.lines = lines  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        return obj


_Cursor = namedtuple("Cursor", ["x", "y"])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ANSI escape sequence handling (used to build a readable transcript)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(
    "\x1b(?:"
    r"\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\?)"  # OSC ... (BEL | ST)
    r"|\[[\x30-\x3f]*[\x20-\x2f]*[\x40-\x7e]"  # CSI ... final
    r"|[P78^_][^\x1b]*(?:\x1b\\)"  # DCS / SOS / PM / APC ... ST
    r"|[\x20-\x2f]*[\x30-\x7e]"  # any other escape sequence
    ")"
)

# Control characters that carry no meaning in a plain-text transcript.
_JUNK_CONTROL_RE = re.compile(r"[\x00\x07\x0b\x0c\x0e\x0f\x1a\x7f]")

_DEFAULT_PATH = "/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

# cursor-key sequences (normal mode) and their application-mode (SS3) form
_CURSOR_KEYS_NORMAL = ("\x1b[A", "\x1b[B", "\x1b[C", "\x1b[D", "\x1b[H", "\x1b[F")
_CURSOR_KEYS_APP = ("\x1bOA", "\x1bOB", "\x1bOC", "\x1bOD", "\x1bOH", "\x1bOF")
_NORMAL_TO_APP = dict(zip(_CURSOR_KEYS_NORMAL, _CURSOR_KEYS_APP))

_SPECIAL_KEYS: Dict[str, str] = {
    "enter": "\r",
    "return": "\r",
    "cr": "\r",
    "newline": "\r",
    "linefeed": "\n",
    "tab": "\t",
    "shift+tab": "\x1b[Z",
    "backtab": "\x1b[Z",
    "esc": "\x1b",
    "escape": "\x1b",
    "space": " ",
    "backspace": "\x7f",
    "bs": "\x7f",
    "delete": "\x1b[3~",
    "del": "\x1b[3~",
    "insert": "\x1b[2~",
    "home": "\x1b[H",
    "end": "\x1b[F",
    "begin": "\x1b[H",
    "up": "\x1b[A",
    "down": "\x1b[B",
    "right": "\x1b[C",
    "forward": "\x1b[C",
    "left": "\x1b[D",
    "back": "\x1b[D",
    "pageup": "\x1b[5~",
    "pgup": "\x1b[5~",
    "pagedown": "\x1b[6~",
    "pgdn": "\x1b[6~",
    "f1": "\x1bOP",
    "f2": "\x1bOQ",
    "f3": "\x1bOR",
    "f4": "\x1bOS",
    "f5": "\x1b[15~",
    "f6": "\x1b[17~",
    "f7": "\x1b[18~",
    "f8": "\x1b[19~",
    "f9": "\x1b[20~",
    "f10": "\x1b[21~",
    "f11": "\x1b[23~",
    "f12": "\x1b[24~",
}


def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove ANSI/VT escape sequences from *text*."""
    return _ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.sub("", text)


def _clean_output(data: bytes, encoding: str = "utf-8") -> str:
    """Turn raw pty output into a readable, newline-normalised transcript."""
    text = data.decode(encoding, "replace")
    text = _strip_ansi(text)
    text = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    text = _JUNK_CONTROL_RE.sub("", text)
    return text


def _key_name_to_sequence(key: str) -> str:
    """Translate a key name such as ``"ctrl+c"`` or ``"enter"`` into the
    byte sequence a real terminal sends for that key."""
    name = str(key).strip().lower().replace("_", "+").replace("-", "+")
    if name in _SPECIAL_KEYS:
        return _SPECIAL_KEYS[name]
    if name.startswith("ctrl+") or name.startswith("control+") or name.startswith("c+"):
        prefix = "ctrl+" if name.startswith("ctrl+") else (
            "control+" if name.startswith("control+") else "c+"
        )
        ch = name[len(prefix):]
        if len(ch) == 1 and "a" <= ch <= "z":
            return chr(ord(ch) - 96)
        if len(ch) == 1 and "0" <= ch <= "9":
            return chr((ord(ch) - ord("0") + 32) % 128)
        if ch == "space":
            return "\x00"
        if ch == "[":
            return "\x1b"
        if ch == "\\":
            return "\x1c"
        if ch == "]":
            return "\x1d"
        if ch == "^":
            return "\x1e"
        if ch == "_":
            return "\x1f"
        raise HeadlessTerminalError("unknown key: {0!r}".format(key))
    if name.startswith("alt+") or name.startswith("meta+") or name.startswith("esc+"):
        return "\x1b" + str(key).strip()[4:]
    # fall back: the key *is* the characters to type
    return str(key)


class _DecckmTracker:
    """Incremental scanner for the DEC private "application cursor keys"
    mode (DECCKM, ``CSI ? 1 h`` / ``CSI ? 1 l``).

    Full-screen programs (vim, less, anything curses based) switch the
    terminal into this mode; while it is active a real terminal sends
    ``SS3`` sequences (``ESC O A``) for the cursor keys instead of
    ``CSI`` sequences (``ESC [ A``).
    """

    _GROUND, _ESC, _CSI, _CSI_PRIVATE, _CSI_OTHER = range(5)

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.application_cursor_keys = False
        self._state = self._GROUND
        self._params = ""

    def feed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        for byte in data:
            state = self._state
            if state == self._GROUND:
                if byte == 0x1B:
                    self._state = self._ESC
            elif state == self._ESC:
                if byte == 0x5B:  # '['
                    self._state = self._CSI
                elif byte == 0x1B:
                    self._state = self._ESC
                else:
                    self._state = self._GROUND
            elif state == self._CSI:
                if byte == 0x3F:  # '?'
                    self._params = ""
                    self._state = self._CSI_PRIVATE
                elif 0x30 <= byte <= 0x3F:
                    self._state = self._CSI_OTHER
                elif 0x40 <= byte <= 0x7E:
                    self._state = self._GROUND
                elif byte == 0x1B:
                    self._state = self._ESC
                # intermediates / other: stay
            elif state == self._CSI_PRIVATE:
                if 0x30 <= byte <= 0x3F:  # parameter bytes
                    self._params += chr(byte)
                elif byte in (0x68, 0x6C):  # 'h' (set) / 'l' (reset)
                    modes = [p for p in self._params.split(";") if p != ""]
                    if "1" in modes:
                        self.application_cursor_keys = byte == 0x68
                    self._state = self._GROUND
                elif 0x40 <= byte <= 0x7E:  # any other final byte
                    self._state = self._GROUND
                elif byte == 0x1B:
                    self._state = self._ESC
                # intermediates: stay
            else:  # _CSI_OTHER
                if 0x40 <= byte <= 0x7E:
                    self._state = self._GROUND
                elif byte == 0x1B:
                    self._state = self._ESC


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fallback screen (only used when pyte is not installed)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _FallbackScreen:
    """A very small VT-screen approximation used when ``pyte`` is missing.

    It understands plain text, carriage returns, line feeds, tabs and
    backspaces, which is enough for ordinary command output.
    """

    def __init__(self, columns: int = 80, lines: int = 24):
        self.columns = columns
        self.lines = lines
        self._rows: List[List[str]] = [[" "] * columns for _ in range(lines)]
        self._x = 0
        self._y = 0
        self.cursor = _Cursor(0, 0)

    # -- api compatible with the parts of pyte we use ----------------------
    def feed(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        text = _strip_ansi(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        for char in text:
            self._put(char)

    def resize(self, lines: Optional[int] = None, columns: Optional[int] = None) -> None:
        if lines is not None:
            self.lines = lines
        if columns is not None:
            self.columns = columns
        rows: List[List[str]] = []
        for index in range(self.lines):
            old = self._rows[index] if index < len(self._rows) else []
            rows.append((old[: self.columns] + [" "] * self.columns)[: self.columns])
        self._rows = rows
        self._x = min(self._x, self.columns - 1)
        self._y = min(self._y, self.lines - 1)
        self.cursor = _Cursor(self._x, self._y)

    @property
    def display(self) -> List[str]:
        return ["".join(row) for row in self._rows]

    # -- internals ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _put(self, char: str) -> None:
        if char == "\n":
            self._x = 0
            self._index()
        elif char == "\r":
            self._x = 0
        elif char == "\b":
            self._x = max(0, self._x - 1)
        elif char == "\t":
            self._x = min(self.columns - 1, (self._x // 8 + 1) * 8)
        elif char >= " ":
            if not 0 <= self._y < len(self._rows):
                self._y = max(0, len(self._rows) - 1)
            row = self._rows[self._y]
            if self._x >= len(row):
                row.extend([" "] * (self._x - len(row) + 1))
            row[self._x] = char
            self._x += 1
            if self._x >= self.columns:
                self._x = 0
                self._index()
        self.cursor = _Cursor(self._x, self._y)

    def _index(self) -> None:
        self._y += 1
        if self._y >= self.lines:
            self._rows.pop(0)
            self._rows.append([" "] * self.columns)
            self._y = self.lines - 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Process bookkeeping (kept separate from the terminal object so that the
# terminal can be garbage-collected while its reader thread is running)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _ProcessState:
    """Everything needed to control / reap the shell process."""

    def __init__(self, pid: int, master_fd: int):
        self.pid = pid
        self.master_fd = master_fd
        self.closed = False
        self.eof = False
        self.exit_status: Optional[int] = None
        self._exit_lock = threading.RLock()

    # -- fd -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def close_fd(self) -> None:
        fd, self.master_fd = self.master_fd, None
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                os.close(fd)  # delivers SIGHUP to the session
            except OSError:
                pass

    # -- reaping -------------------------------------------------------------
    def reap(self, blocking_for: float = 0.0) -> Optional[int]:
        with self._exit_lock:
            if self.exit_status is not None:
                return self.exit_status
            deadline = time.monotonic() + blocking_for
            while True:
                try:
                    pid, status = os.waitpid(self.pid, os.WNOHANG)
                except ChildProcessError:
                    # already reaped somewhere else
                    self.exit_status = 0
                    break
                except InterruptedError:  # pragma: no cover
                    continue
                if pid == self.pid:
                    self.exit_status = status
                    break
                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    break
                time.sleep(0.02)
            return self.exit_status

    def decoded_exit_status(self) -> Optional[int]:
        status = self.exit_status
        if status is None:
            return None
        if os.WIFEXITED(status):
            return os.WEXITSTATUS(status)
        if os.WIFSIGNALED(status):
            return -os.WTERMSIG(status)
        return status

    # -- signalling ----------------------------------------------------------
    def signal_group(self, sig: int) -> None:
        try:
            os.killpg(self.pid, sig)
            return
        except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError):
            pass
        try:
            os.kill(self.pid, sig)
        except OSError:
            pass

    # -- shutdown ------------------------------------------------------------
    def shutdown(self, reader: Optional[threading.Thread] = None) -> None:
        """Stop the reader thread, close the pty and kill the process group."""
        self.closed = True
        if (
            reader is not None
            and reader.is_alive()
            and threading.current_thread() is not reader
        ):
            reader.join(timeout=1.0)
        # Closing the master makes the kernel send SIGHUP to the session.
        self.close_fd()
        if self.reap(blocking_for=0.4) is None:
            self.signal_group(signal.SIGTERM)
            if self.reap(blocking_for=0.4) is None:
                self.signal_group(signal.SIGKILL)
                self.reap(blocking_for=0.4)


def _reader_loop(term_ref: "weakref.ReferenceType[HeadlessTerminal]", fd: int,
                 state: _ProcessState) -> None:
    """Background reader: keeps the pty drained and updates the screen.

    Only a *weak* reference to the terminal object is held while waiting,
    so an unclosed terminal can still be garbage-collected (which shuts
    the pty and the shell down).
    """
    while not state.closed:
        # -- wait for output (no strong reference held while waiting) ------
        try:
            ready, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.05)
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            break
        if not ready:
            if term_ref() is None:  # terminal was garbage-collected
                break
            continue
        try:
            data = os.read(fd, 65536)
        except InterruptedError:  # pragma: no cover
            continue
        except OSError:
            break
        if not data:
            break
        term = term_ref()
        if term is None:  # pragma: no cover - collected mid-read
            break
        term._ingest(data)
        del term  # drop the strong reference before waiting again
    state.eof = True
    term = term_ref()
    if term is not None:  # make sure we do not leave a zombie behind
        term._reap(blocking_for=0.2)
        del term


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The terminal itself
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class HeadlessTerminal(BaseTerminal):
    """A headless terminal emulator running an interactive ``bash`` shell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    command:
        Program to run inside the terminal.  ``None`` (the default) starts
        an interactive ``bash`` shell.  A string is run with ``bash -i -c``
        and a list is used as the ``argv`` directly.
    cols, rows:
        Size of the terminal window (default 80x24).
    env:
        Extra environment variables merged over the current environment.
    cwd:
        Working directory for the shell.
    encoding:
        Encoding used to decode the terminal output (default ``utf-8``).
    term:
        Value of the ``TERM`` environment variable (default
        ``xterm-256color``).
    """

    # after sending keystrokes, keep waiting for late output until the
    # terminal has been quiet for this long (bounded, so it never hangs)
    _DRAIN_QUIET = 0.05
    _DRAIN_LIMIT = 0.6

    def __init__(
        self,
        command: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None,
        cols: Optional[int] = None,
        rows: Optional[int] = None,
        env: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
        cwd: Optional[str] = None,
        encoding: str = "utf-8",
        term: Optional[str] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()

        # -- forgiving keyword aliases --------------------------------------
        if cols is None:
            cols = kwargs.pop("columns", kwargs.pop("width", None))
        if rows is None:
            rows = kwargs.pop("lines", kwargs.pop("height", None))
        if command is None:
            command = kwargs.pop(
                "cmd",
                kwargs.pop("argv", kwargs.pop("shell", kwargs.pop("program", None))),
            )
        if env is None:
            env = kwargs.pop("environment", None)
        if cwd is None:
            cwd = kwargs.pop(
                "working_dir", kwargs.pop("workdir", kwargs.pop("directory", None))
            )
        if term is None:
            term = kwargs.pop("term_type", kwargs.pop("TERM", None))
        self._default_timeout = float(kwargs.pop("timeout", 10.0))
        # any remaining keyword arguments are ignored on purpose (forward
        # compatibility with alternative constructor signatures)

        self._cols = max(2, int(cols)) if cols else 80
        self._rows = max(2, int(rows)) if rows else 24
        self._encoding = encoding or "utf-8"
        self._bash_path = shutil.which("bash") or "/bin/bash"

        # -- state -----------------------------------------------------------
        self._raw = bytearray()          # every byte ever printed by the pty
        self._lock = threading.RLock()   # protects _raw / screen / stream
        self._write_errors: List[BaseException] = []
        self._expect_pos = 0
        self._read_new_pos = 0
        self._decckm = _DecckmTracker()
        self._created_at = time.monotonic()

        child_env = self._build_env(env, term)
        argv = self._build_argv(command)

        pid, master_fd = pty.fork()
        if pid == 0:  # ----- child: becomes the interactive shell -----
            try:
                if cwd:
                    os.chdir(cwd)
                os.execve(argv[0], argv, child_env)
            except BaseException as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exec failure
                try:
                    os.write(
                        2,
                        "headless_terminal: cannot exec {0!r}: {1}\n".format(
                            argv, exc
                        ).encode("utf-8", "replace"),
                    )
                except OSError:
                    pass
            os._exit(127)

        # ----- parent -----
        self._state = _ProcessState(pid, master_fd)
        try:
            self._set_winsize(self._rows, self._cols)
        except OSError:  # pragma: no cover
            pass

        # virtual screen: a real terminal emulator (with scrollback)
        if pyte is not None:
            self._screen = pyte.HistoryScreen(self._cols, self._rows, history=1000)
            self._stream = pyte.ByteStream(self._screen)
        else:  # pragma: no cover - pyte is normally installed
            self._screen = _FallbackScreen(self._cols, self._rows)
            self._stream = self._screen  # type: ignore[assignment]

        self._reader = threading.Thread(
            target=_reader_loop,
            args=(weakref.ref(self), master_fd, self._state),
            name="headless-terminal-reader-{0}".format(pid),
            daemon=True,
        )
        # when the terminal is garbage-collected (or the interpreter exits)
        # the pty is closed and the whole process group is shut down
        self._finalizer = weakref.finalize(self, self._state.shutdown, self._reader)
        self._reader.start()

        # give the shell a chance to start up, print its prompt and source
        # the startup files before the first keystrokes arrive
        self._wait_for_initial_output()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # BaseTerminal interface
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def send_keystrokes(self, keystrokes: str, wait_sec: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Send *keystrokes* to the terminal.

        Args:
            keystrokes: The keystrokes to send to the terminal.  Plain
                characters are typed literally; ``"\\n"`` (or ``"\\r"``) is
                the Enter key; control keys are sent as their control
                character (``"\\x03"`` = Ctrl-C, ``"\\x04"`` = Ctrl-D,
                ``"\\x1a"`` = Ctrl-Z, ...) and escape sequences such as
                ``"\\x1b[A"`` (Up arrow) are passed through verbatim.
            wait_sec: The number of seconds to wait for the command to
                complete.
        """
        data = self._keystrokes_to_bytes(keystrokes)
        self._write(data)
        try:
            wait = float(wait_sec)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            wait = 0.0
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep(wait)
        # capture any output that is still in flight (bounded by a short
        # quiet period, so this never hangs)
        self._drain(quiet=self._DRAIN_QUIET, limit=self._DRAIN_LIMIT)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

        if cols is not None:
            self._cols = max(2, int(cols))

    def expect(self, pattern, timeout: Optional[float] = None):
        """Wait until *pattern* (a regex or a literal string) appears in the
        output and return the match object.

        Raises :class:`TerminalTimeout` if the pattern does not show up in
        time.
        """
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = self._default_timeout
        if isinstance(pattern, re.Pattern):
            regex = pattern
        elif isinstance(pattern, (list, tuple)):
            regex = re.compile(
                "|".join("(?:{0})".format(re.escape(str(p))) for p in pattern)
            )
        else:
            regex = re.compile(str(pattern))

        start = self._expect_pos
        deadline = time.monotonic() + float(timeout)
        while True:
            text = self.output
            match = regex.search(text, start)
            if match is not None:
                self._expect_pos = match.end()
                return match
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise TerminalTimeout(
                    "pattern {0!r} not found in terminal output after {1}s".format(
                        pattern, timeout

                )
            time.sleep(0.02)

    # Process management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def is_alive(self) -> bool:
        """``True`` while the shell (or its foreground program) is running."""
        if self._state.exit_status is not None:
            return False
        return self._state.reap() is None

    @property
    def alive(self) -> bool:
        """Alias of :meth:`is_alive`."""
        return self.is_alive()

    @property
    def pid(self) -> int:
        """Process id of the shell."""
        return self._state.pid

    @property
    def exit_status(self) -> Optional[int]:
        """Exit status of the shell (``None`` while it is still running)."""
        self._state.reap()
        return self._state.decoded_exit_status()

    returncode = exit_status
    exit_code = exit_status

    def wait(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[int]:
        """Wait for the shell to exit and return its exit status."""
        deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
        while True:
            if self._state.reap(blocking_for=0.1) is not None:
                return self.exit_status
            if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                return None
            time.sleep(0.02)

    def terminate(self, timeout: float = 1.0) -> None:
        """Politely terminate the shell and everything it started."""
        self._state.signal_group(signal.SIGTERM)
        if self._state.reap(blocking_for=timeout) is None:
            self.kill()

    def kill(self) -> None:
        """Forcefully kill the shell and everything it started."""
        self._state.signal_group(signal.SIGKILL)
        self._state.reap(blocking_for=0.5)

    def close(self, timeout: float = 1.0) -> None:
        """Shut the terminal down and reap the shell process.

        The shell is first given the chance to exit on its own (so it can
        run its exit handlers); after that the pty is closed (SIGHUP) and,
        if need be, the process group is terminated.
        """
        state = self._state
        if state.closed:
            state.reap(blocking_for=0.1)
            return

        # 1) ask the shell nicely to quit
        if state.master_fd is not None:
            try:
                os.write(state.master_fd, b"exit\r")
            except OSError:
                pass
            state.reap(blocking_for=min(timeout, 0.8))

        # 2) close the pty / kill the process group (at most once)
        self._finalizer()

    shutdown = close
    stop = close

    # context manager ---------------------------------------------------------
    def __enter__(self) -> "HeadlessTerminal":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        state = "closed" if self._state.closed else (
            "alive" if self.is_alive() else "exited"
        )
        return "<HeadlessTerminal pid={0} size={1}x{2} {3}>".format(
            self._state.pid, self._cols, self._rows, state

    # internals
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _build_argv(self, command) -> List[str]:
        if command is None:
            # interactive bash: sources /etc/bash.bashrc and ~/.bashrc
            return [self._bash_path, "-i"]
        if isinstance(command, (list, tuple)):
            argv = [str(part) for part in command]
            if not argv:
                raise HeadlessTerminalError("empty command")
            resolved = shutil.which(argv[0]) or argv[0]
            return [resolved] + argv[1:]
        if isinstance(command, str):
            return [self._bash_path, "-i", "-c", command]
        raise HeadlessTerminalError("unsupported command: {0!r}".format(command))

    def _build_env(self, env, term) -> Dict[str, str]:
        child_env = dict(os.environ)
        if env:
            child_env.update({str(k): str(v) for k, v in env.items()})
        term_name = term or "xterm-256color"
        if not child_env.get("TERM") or child_env.get("TERM") == "dumb":
            child_env["TERM"] = term_name
        child_env.setdefault("HOME", os.path.expanduser("~") or "/root")
        child_env.setdefault("USER", child_env.get("LOGNAME") or "root")
        child_env.setdefault("LOGNAME", child_env.get("USER") or "root")
        child_env.setdefault("SHELL", self._bash_path)
        child_env.setdefault("PATH", _DEFAULT_PATH)
        # make sure python subprocesses do not buffer their output forever
        child_env.setdefault("PYTHONUNBUFFERED", "1")
        return child_env

    def _set_winsize(self, rows: int, cols: int) -> None:
        fd = self._state.master_fd
        if fd is None:
            return
        winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0)
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)

    def _keystrokes_to_bytes(self, keystrokes) -> bytes:
        if keystrokes is None:
            return b""
        if isinstance(keystrokes, (bytes, bytearray)):
            data = bytes(keystrokes)
        elif isinstance(keystrokes, str):
            data = self._translate_cursor_keys(keystrokes).encode(self._encoding)
        else:
            data = self._translate_cursor_keys(str(keystrokes)).encode(self._encoding)
        # A real terminal sends CR when Enter is pressed; the tty line
        # discipline (ICRNL) translates it to NL for the reading program.
        data = data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\r").replace(b"\n", b"\r")
        return data

    def _translate_cursor_keys(self, text: str) -> str:
        """While the foreground program keeps the terminal in *application
        cursor keys* mode (DECCKM), a real terminal sends ``SS3`` sequences
        for the cursor keys -- do the same."""
        if not self._decckm.application_cursor_keys:
            return text
        for normal, application in _NORMAL_TO_APP.items():
            if normal in text:
                text = text.replace(normal, application)
        return text

    def _write(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        fd = self._state.master_fd
        if fd is None or self._state.closed:
            return  # terminal is gone; ignore writes
        view = memoryview(data)
        while view:
            try:
                written = os.write(fd, view)
            except BlockingIOError:  # pty input buffer full
                try:
                    select.select([], [fd], [], 0.1)
                except (OSError, ValueError):
                    break
                continue
            except OSError as exc:
                # the shell most likely died; remember but do not crash
                if not self._write_errors or self._write_errors[-1] != exc:
                    self._write_errors.append(exc)
                break
            view = view[written:]

    def _ingest(self, data: bytes) -> None:
        """Called by the reader thread for every chunk of terminal output."""
        with self._lock:
            self._raw.extend(data)
            try:
                self._decckm.feed(data)
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - never crash the reader
                pass
            try:
                self._stream.feed(data)
            except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - never crash the reader
                pass

    def _reap(self, blocking_for: float = 0.0) -> Optional[int]:
        return self._state.reap(blocking_for=blocking_for)

    def _drain(self, quiet: float = 0.05, limit: float = 0.5) -> None:
        """Wait until the terminal has produced no output for *quiet*
        seconds, at most *limit* seconds in total."""
        deadline = time.monotonic() + max(0.0, limit)
        last_size = len(self._raw)
        last_change = time.monotonic()
        while True:
            time.sleep(0.01)
            now = time.monotonic()
            size = len(self._raw)
            if size != last_size:
                last_size = size
                last_change = now
                if now >= deadline:
                    return
                continue
            if now - last_change >= quiet or now >= deadline:
                return

    def _wait_for_initial_output(self, timeout: float = 3.0) -> None:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while not self._raw:
            if self._state.eof or self._state.exit_status is not None:
                break
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                break
            time.sleep(0.005)
        if self._raw:
            self._drain(quiet=0.1, limit=1.0)

    def _render_screen(
        self, include_history: bool = False, rstrip: bool = True
    ) -> _ScreenText:
        with self._lock:
            rows = [
                "".join(chars) if not isinstance(chars, str) else chars
                for chars in self._screen.display
            ]
            cursor = getattr(self._screen, "cursor", None)
            columns = getattr(self._screen, "columns", self._cols)
            lines_count = getattr(self._screen, "lines", self._rows)
            history_rows: List[str] = []
            if include_history:
                history = getattr(self._screen, "history", None)
                top = getattr(history, "top", None) if history else None
                if top:
                    for line in top:
                        try:
                            history_rows.append(
                                "".join(char.data for char in line.values())
                            )
                        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
                            pass
        display = [row.rstrip() for row in rows]
        all_rows = history_rows + display
        text = "\n".join(all_rows)
        if rstrip:
            text = text.rstrip("\n")
        cursor_pos = None
        if cursor is not None:
            cursor_pos = _Cursor(
                int(getattr(cursor, "x", 0)), int(getattr(cursor, "y", 0))
            )
        return _ScreenText(
            text,
            display=all_rows,
            cursor=cursor_pos,
            columns=int(columns or self._cols),
            lines=int(lines_count or self._rows),
        )

Implemented `HeadlessTerminal(BaseTerminal)` in `/app/headless_terminal.py` (importable as `from headless_terminal import HeadlessTerminal`), with dependencies (`pyte`, `pexpect`) installed into the system Python.

## Design

A real pseudo-terminal (`pty.fork()`) whose slave is the controlling tty of an **interactive `bash -i`** shell. A background reader thread continuously drains the pty master, feeding a `pyte` virtual terminal emulator (with scrollback) and accumulating the raw output — so interactive programs never block and no output is lost.

## Required functionality

- **Mimics a terminal**: real pty with job control, echo, prompt, 80×24 window (resizable, `TIOCSWINSZ`), `TERM=xterm-256color`; full VT emulation via pyte including the **alternate screen buffer** (`?1049h/l`) so full-screen apps (vim/less/curses) draw on their own screen and restore it on exit, and **DECCKM tracking** so cursor keys are sent as `SS3` sequences (`\x1bOA`) while an app is in application-cursor-keys mode — exactly what a real terminal does.
- **Commands via typing + Enter**: `send_keystrokes("echo hi
", wait_sec=1.0)`; `
` is translated to `` (Enter sends CR; the tty's ICRNL converts it for the app); after sending, waits `wait_sec` then drains until output is quiet (bounded, never hangs).
- **Interactive programs**: continuous background reading, screen-state rendering (`screen`, `display`, `cursor`), `expect()`/`wait_for()` pattern matching, and graceful handling of continuously-updating programs (top-style loops).
- **Modifier keys**: raw bytes go straight to the pty, so `\x03` (Ctrl-C/SIGINT), `\x04` (Ctrl-D/EOF), `\x1a` (Ctrl-Z), `\x15` (Ctrl-U), `	` (Tab completion), `\x7f` (Backspace), `\x1b[A` (Up) etc. all work; named keys too (`press("ctrl+c")`, `press("enter")`).
- **Startup files**: the shell is interactive, so `/etc/bash.bashrc` and `~/.bashrc` are sourced (verified with exported vars and aliases).

## Extras

Rich observation API (`output`/`text`/`log`/`transcript`, `raw_output`, `screen`, `lines`, `get_output()`, `read()`, `read_new()`, …), process management (`is_alive`, `wait`, `exit_status`, `close`, `terminate`, `kill`, context manager), GC-safe teardown via `weakref.finalize` (no leaked bash/child processes even without explicit `close()`), configurable `command`/`cols`/`rows`/`env`/`cwd`, and a pyte-free fallback screen.

    return values - baseline


def analyze(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[StationResult]:
    """Compute per-station statistics for every station present in the data."""
    results: list[StationResult] = []
    # Grouping iteration works directly in Python 3 (no ``.iteritems()`` needed).
    for station_id, group in frame.groupby("station_id", sort=True):
        mean_temperature = float(group["temperature"].mean())
        station_name = str(group["station_name"].iloc[0])
        results.append(
            StationResult(
                station_id=int(station_id),
                station_name=station_name,
                observations=int(len(group)),
                mean_temperature=mean_temperature,
            )
        )
    return results


def _plot_settings(config: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Merge the ``[plotting]`` section of the config over the defaults."""
    settings: dict[str, object] = dict(DEFAULT_PLOT_SETTINGS)
    if "plotting.figure_width" in config:
        settings["figure_width"] = int(config["plotting.figure_width"])
    if "plotting.figure_height" in config:
        settings["figure_height"] = int(config["plotting.figure_height"])
    if "plotting.dpi" in config:
        settings["dpi"] = int(config["plotting.dpi"])
    if "plotting.output_path" in config:
        settings["output_path"] = config["plotting.output_path"]
    if "plotting.color_scheme" in config:
        settings["color_scheme"] = config["plotting.color_scheme"]
    return settings


def create_visualization(
    frame: pd.DataFrame,
    results: Sequence[StationResult],
    config: dict[str, str],
) -> list[Path]:
    """Optionally render one PNG per station. Returns the written file paths."""
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")  # headless-safe backend; no blocking plt.show()
    import matplotlib.dates as mdates
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    settings = _plot_settings(config)
    colours = [c.strip() for c in str(settings["color_scheme"]).split(",") if c.strip()]
    output_dir = Path(str(settings["output_path"])).expanduser()
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    written: list[Path] = []
    for index, result in enumerate(results):
        group = frame[frame["station_id"] == result.station_id]
        anomalies = calculate_anomalies(group["temperature"])

        figure, axis = plt.subplots(
            figsize=(float(settings["figure_width"]), float(settings["figure_height"])),
        )
        # ``plot_date`` is deprecated; a normal ``plot`` handles datetimes fine.
        axis.plot(group["date"].to_numpy(), anomalies, "-", color=colours[index % len(colours)])
        axis.axhline(0.0, color="grey", linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--")
        axis.set_title(
            f"Temperature Anomalies - Station {result.station_id}", fontsize=16, fontweight="bold"
        )
        axis.set_xlabel("Date")
        axis.set_ylabel("Anomaly (°C)")
        axis.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y-%m"))
        axis.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(interval=1))
        figure.autofmt_xdate()
        figure.tight_layout()

        # pathlib keeps unicode-safe filenames on every platform.
        out_path = output_dir / f"climate_plot_station_{result.station_id}.png"
        figure.savefig(out_path, dpi=int(settings["dpi"]))
        plt.close(figure)
        written.append(out_path)
        LOGGER.info("Wrote plot to %s", out_path)

    return written


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Modernized climate data analysis (Python 3).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--csv",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_CSV_PATH,
        help=f"Path to the climate CSV file (default: {DEFAULT_CSV_PATH})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH,
        help=f"Path to the INI config file (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--plot",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also write a PNG plot per station (headless, no window is opened).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable verbose logging.",
    )
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.DEBUG if args.verbose else logging.WARNING,
        format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s",
        stream=sys.stderr,
    )

    print("Starting climate analysis...")
    try:
        config = load_config(args.config)
        frame = load_temperature_data(args.csv)
        results = analyze(frame)
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError, OSError, configparser.Error) as error:
        # Modern exception handling: ``except ... as error``.
        print(f"Error occurred: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    for result in results:
        print(result.summary_line)

    if args.plot:
        try:
            for path in create_visualization(frame, results, config):
                print(f"Plot written to {path}")
        except ImportError:
            print("matplotlib is not installed - skipping plots", file=sys.stderr)

    print("Analysis completed successfully!")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Modernized climate data analysis script (Python 3.10+).

Modernization notes
-------------------
Every Python-2-only construct from the legacy script was replaced by its
current equivalent:

* ``from __future__`` imports and statement-style printing  ->  ``print()`` and f-strings
* the legacy INI-parser shim                               ->  stdlib ``configparser``
* manual byte-to-text decoding                              ->  native ``str`` + explicit UTF-8

* legacy pickle / HTTP / string-buffer modules              ->  dropped (unused here)
* removed NumPy scalar aliases                              ->  ``float`` / ``np.float64``
* deprecated pandas groupby iteration and date parsing      ->  direct iteration, ``parse_dates``
* deprecated matplotlib date plotting and blocking display  ->  ``ax.plot`` + non-interactive backend
* hardcoded absolute string paths                           ->  ``pathlib.Path`` (unicode-safe)

Usage
-----

    python3 analyze_climate_modern.py --plot                # also write PNG plots
